body:
# Telegraph Protocol miner config.
#
# registrationId 111 (2026-08-18) was rejected on-chain: "endpoints.0:
# Additional property input_schema is not allowed" / same for output_schema.
# Confirmed against the real docs.telegraphprotocol.com/docs/miners/
# yaml-config page (not the 2026-08-14 cached read, which missed this):
# the endpoints[] schema is a closed set (path, external_path, method,
# description, endpoint_base_url, content_type, multipart_fields,
# param_map only, additionalProperties: false) — input_schema/output_schema
# are top-level-only fields, not per-endpoint. Fixed below by moving them
# to the top level.
#
# `id: 0` was WRONG — the 2026-08-14 read above conflated this field with
# the on-chain registrationId. They are two different keys. This YAML `id`
# is the routing key for /engine/v1/ask/{id} and must be globally unused;
# `id: 0` collided with active miner "lacre-meteo" and caused registration
# 125 to be REJECTED on 2026-08-20 (confirmed live on
# explorer.telegraphprotocol.com/miners/125). Fixed 2026-08-24: id changed
# to 9002 (checked unused against /miner-dispatcher/integrations).
#
# Still TODO before registering on-chain:
#   - This file itself must be hosted at a public URL (IPFS recommended)
#     and its SHA-256 hash committed on-chain — see miner-registration docs.
#   - feeAddress (MACHINA payout wallet) and minPriceUsdc (floor price,
#     min $0.01) still need to be decided and supplied to registerMiner —
#     not part of this YAML, passed directly in the registration tx.

version: "1"
kind: miner
id: 9002
slug: txlens
protocol: generic
name: TxLens
description: >
  TxLens provides live, verifiable answers to on-chain and market questions
  from authoritative sources. Covering 72 intents across blockchain, finance,
  weather, content, security, and general intelligence domains—each answer
  includes source attribution and fetch timestamps for transparency.
base_url: https://telegraph-onchain-tx-lookup-miner.onrender.com

auth:
  type: none

endpoints:
  - path: /check-tx
    external_path: /check-tx
    method: GET
    intents: [ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP]
    description: >
      ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP. Answers "is transaction 0xabc... confirmed or did
      it fail", "what did this tx hash do", "what is the status of this
      transaction on Base". Takes a specific transaction reference and
      returns its details, status and effects: confirmed, reverted, pending
      or not_found, plus from, to, value_wei, value_eth, block_number,
      block_hash, receipt_status, and the decoded contract method where the
      calldata identifies one. Confidence scales with confirmation depth.
      Params: tx_hash (required, 0x-prefixed, 64 hex characters), chain
      (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth).
  - path: /gas-price
    external_path: /gas-price
    method: GET
    intents: [GAS_PRICE]
    description: >
      GAS_PRICE. Answers "what is gas right now on Ethereum", "how much does
      a transfer cost on Polygon", "are fees high on Base". Returns the
      current transaction fee level on a named chain in wei and gwei, plus
      the estimated USD cost of a standard 21,000-gas transfer. This is the
      fee to transact, not the price of the chain's token, which is
      CRYPTO_PRICE. Params: chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum,
      polygon, default eth).
  - path: /wallet-balance
    external_path: /wallet-balance
    method: GET
    intents: [WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK]
    description: >
      WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. Answers "how much ETH does 0xabc... hold", "what
      is the USDC balance of this address on Arbitrum". Takes a specific
      blockchain address and returns its current native-coin or ERC-20 token
      balance on a named chain. Params: address (required, 0x-prefixed, 40
      hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum,
      polygon, default eth), token (optional, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex
      characters, an ERC-20 contract address; when supplied, returns that
      token's balance instead of the chain's native coin).
  - path: /token-holders
    external_path: /token-holders
    method: GET
    intents: [TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT]
    description: >
      TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT. Answers "how many wallets hold this token", "how
      many distinct addresses own 0xabc...". Takes a specific token contract
      address and returns the count of distinct holding addresses. This is a
      holder count, not price, supply or market data. Params: token
      (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of
      eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth).
  - path: /tvl
    external_path: /tvl
    method: GET
    intents: [TVL_LOOKUP]
    description: >
      TVL_LOOKUP. Answers "what is the TVL of Aave", "how much value is
      locked in Uniswap", "what is total value locked on Ethereum". Takes a
      named DeFi protocol, pool or chain and returns the total value locked
      in it in USD. This is value locked, not market capitalisation. When
      both a protocol and a chain are supplied it returns that protocol's
      TVL on that chain alongside its total across all chains. Params:
      exactly one of protocol (a DefiLlama protocol slug, e.g. "uniswap") or
      tvl_chain (a free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "Ethereum", covering
      DefiLlama's ~460 chains rather than only the five EVM chains above,
      which is why the param name differs from `chain`).
  - path: /crypto-price
    external_path: /crypto-price
    method: GET
    intents: [CRYPTO_PRICE]
    description: >
      CRYPTO_PRICE. Answers "what is Bitcoin worth", "price of ETH in USD",
      "how much is the token at 0xabc... trading for". Names a
      cryptocurrency asset and returns its current USD price, with 24-hour
      change and market cap where the feed supplies them, cross-checked
      across independent sources and reported with a source count. For the
      cost of transacting on a chain use GAS_PRICE instead. Params: either
      coin_id alone, or price_chain together with token. Exactly one of
      those two modes. Any coin named in words goes in coin_id, including a
      coin that shares its name with a chain: ether or Ethereum is
      coin_id="ethereum", and likewise "bitcoin", "solana". price_chain is
      only for pricing one specific contract, is never sent on its own, and
      always needs token (0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, the token's
      contract address) alongside it, as in price_chain="base" with the
      contract to price. It also answers what a coin was worth on a past
      day: send that day as date ("2023-01-01"), in either mode, and the
      answer is the price on that date rather than the price now. Leave
      date off for the current price.
  - path: /stock-price
    external_path: /stock-price
    method: GET
    intents: [STOCK_PRICE]
    description: >
      STOCK_PRICE. Answers "what is Apple trading at", "current share price
      of TSLA", "how much is NVDA stock". Names a listed equity or ticker
      and returns its current USD share price. It also answers what a stock
      was worth on a past day, such as "what did NVDA close at on 15
      January 2024": send that day as date and the answer is the closing
      price on it, naming the last trading day before it when the market
      was shut that day. Params: ticker (required, a stock symbol, e.g.
      "AAPL") and date (optional, a past day as "2024-01-15"; leave it off
      for the current price).
  - path: /ssl-check
    external_path: /ssl-check
    method: GET
    intents: [SSL_VERIFICATION]
    description: >
      SSL_VERIFICATION. Answers "is the SSL certificate for example.com
      valid", "when does this domain's TLS certificate expire", "who issued
      the certificate for this host". Takes a hostname and reports the
      certificate that host is actually serving right now, from a real live
      TLS handshake performed at request time rather than a cached or
      certificate-transparency lookup, which disagree whenever a host still
      serves an old certificate. Reports a named verdict (valid, expired,
      self_signed, hostname_mismatch, untrusted), issuer, validity window,
      days to expiry, how many certificates the server presented and
      whether the chain reaches a trusted root, which name on the
      certificate the request matched, and the TLS version and cipher
      actually negotiated, flagging deprecated TLS 1.0/1.1 that will fail
      for modern clients whatever the certificate says. Params: domain
      (required, a bare hostname such as "example.com", a full URL, a
      host:port pair, or a question naming the domain).
  - path: /weather-forecast
    external_path: /weather-forecast
    method: GET
    intents: [WEATHER_FORECAST]
    description: >
      WEATHER_FORECAST. Answers "what's the weather in Tokyo the next
      three days", "will it rain in London tomorrow", "how windy will it
      be in Cape Town on Friday", "will it snow in Oslo next week", and
      coordinate forms such as "what is the forecast at latitude 14.6042,
      longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?". Accepts coordinates written out in
      full ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon"
      pair, a place name, or the whole question, and answers the specific
      thing asked: the day or window named (right now, today, tonight,
      tomorrow, a weekday, this weekend, this week, in N hours, the next N
      days or hours) and the aspect emphasised (rain, wind, snow, storm,
      freeze, temperature), leading with a direct yes or no on that aspect
      the way a person would answer, then giving the expected condition in
      plain words, temperature range, precipitation total and chance of
      precipitation, snowfall, and peak wind speed with gusts and direction.
      Read live from the forecast service at request time. Params:
      location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name, or a
      whole question), days (optional, 1-16), when (optional, overrides
      the window parsed from the question), focus (optional, one of rain,
      wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature).
  - path: /storm-alert
    external_path: /storm-alert
    method: GET
    intents: [STORM_ALERT]
    description: >
      STORM_ALERT. Reports storm risk at a location over a stated window,
      answering questions of the form "what is the storm risk at latitude
      14.6042, longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?" and "what is the storm risk
      at latitude -5.1486, longitude 119.4319 right now?", as well as
      "is there a storm risk in Miami this weekend". Reports exactly what
      such a question asks for: wind speed, gusts, precipitation, and an
      overall risk between 0 and 1. Accepts coordinates written out in full
      ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon" pair, a
      place name, or the whole question, and reads the window from it
      ("right now", "in N hours", "over the next 48 hours", "this weekend").
      Alongside the 0-1 risk score a contract can threshold on, it returns a
      disruption grade (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/SEVERE) from peak wind gust and
      its Beaufort force named in plain words, sustained wind speed and
      direction, total precipitation, forecast thunderstorm and hail hours,
      and the operational response that grade calls for. The window runs
      from the current hour forward, not from midnight, so the peak gust
      reported is always still ahead. Read live at request time.
      Params: location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name,
      or a whole question), hours (optional, default 48, also read from the
      question).
  - path: /ip-geolocate
    external_path: /ip-geolocate
    method: GET
    intents: [IP_GEOLOCATION]
    description: >
      IP_GEOLOCATION. Answers "where is 8.8.8.8 located", "what country is
      this IP address from", "is this IP a VPN or a datacenter". Takes an
      IPv4 or IPv6 address and reports its country, region, city, postal
      code, coordinates, timezone, and network owner with ASN, plus
      privacy and risk flags saying whether the address is a known proxy
      or VPN exit, a hosting or datacenter network, or a mobile carrier
      network, which is what fraud, bot-screening and geo-gating callers
      actually need. Read live at request time. Confidence is reported as
      0.95 rather than 1.0 because IP geolocation is reliable to the
      country and only approximate to the city. Params: ip (required, a
      bare IPv4 or IPv6 address such as "8.8.8.8" or
      "2001:4860:4860::8888", or a whole question naming one).
  - path: /academic-search
    external_path: /academic-search
    method: GET
    intents: [ACADEMIC_SEARCH]
    description: >
      ACADEMIC_SEARCH. Answers "find papers on federated learning",
      "peer-reviewed research on fraud detection since 2020". Takes a
      topic, or the whole question, and lists peer-reviewed journal
      articles on it in relevance order, with preprints, theses and
      datasets excluded, naming every paper found in the answer itself
      with its title, authors, publishing journal, year, citation count
      and DOI, plus a real excerpt from the leading paper's abstract and a
      note on which of the results is the most cited. A date range stated
      in the question ("since 2020", "between 2010 and 2020") is applied.
      Read live from OpenAlex, with Crossref as a fallback, at request time. Params: topic (required),
      limit (optional, 1-25, default 5), from_year (optional), to_year
      (optional).
  - path: /web-search
    external_path: /web-search
    method: GET
    intents: [WEB_SEARCH]
    description: >
      WEB_SEARCH. Answers an open question of any kind from a live web
      search performed at request time, for questions that have no single
      authoritative feed behind them: "what happened at the summit this
      week", "how does a heat pump work", "will El Nino disrupt shipping
      this season", "what did the company announce". Takes the whole
      question as the caller wrote it and returns a direct written answer
      followed by the sources it drew on, naming the most relevant three
      with their URLs. Questions about current events are searched against
      a news index and questions about markets and company results against
      a finance index, chosen from the wording of the question itself.
      Confidence is reported as 0.9 rather than 1.0 because a synthesized
      web answer is only as reliable as the pages behind it, unlike a chain
      read or a live TLS handshake. For a peer-reviewed literature search
      use ACADEMIC_SEARCH instead, and for a live number such as a price,
      gas fee, balance or forecast use the specific intent for it, which
      reads the value from its own provider rather than from the open web.
      Params: query (required, the whole question), max_results (optional,
      1-20, default 5), topic_mode (optional, one of general, news,
      finance, overriding what the question implies).
  - path: /content-extract
    external_path: /content-extract
    method: GET
    intents: [CONTENT_EXTRACTION]
    description: >
      CONTENT_EXTRACTION. Answers "what does this page say", "extract the
      text from this URL", "summarize the content at this link". Fetches a
      live URL at request time and returns its title and readable text,
      stripped of scripts, navigation, and markup. Params: url (required, a
      full http or https URL, a bare host such as github.com/torvalds, or a
      whole question containing one; also accepted as link or question). If
      the value is a passage of text with no URL, the dates, quantities,
      named entities and events are extracted from the text itself.
  - path: /text-classify
    external_path: /text-classify
    method: GET
    intents: [TEXT_CLASSIFICATION]
    description: >
      TEXT_CLASSIFICATION. Answers "what category is this text", "is this
      email spam or not", "classify this review as positive or negative".
      Takes a piece of text and returns the single best category it
      belongs to, with a brief reason. Params: text (required; also accepted
      as content or input), labels (optional, also accepted as categories or
      classes; comma-separated candidate categories the answer must pick
      from; if omitted, the category is chosen freely).
  - path: /text-generate
    external_path: /text-generate
    method: GET
    intents: [TEXT_GENERATION]
    description: >
      TEXT_GENERATION. Answers "write a short bio for a software
      engineer", "draft a product description for a water bottle". Takes an
      instruction or prompt and writes the requested text directly, with no
      preamble. Params: prompt (required).
  - path: /language-generate
    external_path: /language-generate
    method: GET
    intents: [LANGUAGE_GENERATION]
    description: >
      LANGUAGE_GENERATION. Answers "translate this into French", "rewrite
      this in a formal tone", "paraphrase this sentence". Takes existing
      text and transforms it into another language, tone, or style. Params:
      text (required), target (optional, the target language/tone/style;
      also read from the instruction inside text when omitted).
  - path: /research-synthesis
    external_path: /research-synthesis
    method: GET
    intents: [RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS]
    description: >
      RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS. Answers broader research questions such as "what
      are the main approaches to carbon capture" or "summarize the current
      state of quantum error correction". Combines multiple live web
      sources into one written synthesis, wider and more source-dense than
      WEB_SEARCH. Params: query (required; also q, question, topic, text),
      max_sources (optional, 1-20, default 10; also max_results, limit).
  - path: /cross-chain-state
    external_path: /cross-chain-state
    method: GET
    intents: [CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY]
    description: >
      CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY. Answers "which chains is this address
      active on", "does this wallet exist on Base and Arbitrum", "is this a
      contract on any chain". Checks the same address's native balance and
      contract status on every supported chain at once. Params: address
      (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chains (optional,
      comma-separated list restricting which chains are checked; defaults
      to every RPC-enabled chain). Chains named in the question ("on Base
      and Arbitrum") restrict the check when chains is omitted; chains this
      miner cannot read (Solana, Bitcoin, Optimism) are named as unchecked
      in the answer.
  - path: /event-outcome
    external_path: /event-outcome
    method: GET
    intents: [EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION]
    description: >
      EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION. Answers "did the merger go through", "who
      won the election", "was the proposal approved". Resolves a question
      about whether something happened to a stated outcome from a live web
      search, leading with the verdict (yes/no/winner) before the
      supporting facts. Params: query (required; also q, question, event,
      market). Answer leads with "Yes,", "No,", the winner's name, or "Not
      yet resolved," for events that have not happened; the outcome field
      carries yes/no/unresolved.
  - path: /weather-check
    external_path: /weather-check
    method: GET
    intents: [WEATHER_CHECK]
    description: >
      WEATHER_CHECK. Answers "what's the weather like in Tokyo right now",
      "current temperature in London", "is it raining in Cape Town at the
      moment". Returns a single live current-conditions reading at a named
      place: temperature, apparent temperature, humidity, wind speed and
      direction, precipitation, cloud cover, and plain-words condition, read
      live at request time rather than forecast. Params: location (required,
      a place name, "lat,lon" pair, or a whole question naming the place;
      also accepted as city, place, q, query or question, or as lat/lon or
      latitude/longitude).
  - path: /language-translate
    external_path: /language-translate
    method: GET
    intents: [LANGUAGE_TRANSLATION]
    description: >
      LANGUAGE_TRANSLATION. Answers "translate 'good morning' into Japanese",
      "how do you say thank you in French". Takes text and a target language
      and returns the translation only, with no explanation. Params: text
      (required; a whole instruction such as "Translate 'good morning' into
      Spanish" is accepted and the language is read from it), target
      (optional when the text names the language; also accepted as
      target_language, to, language or langpair such as "en|de").
  - path: /chat-complete
    external_path: /chat-complete
    method: GET
    intents: [CHAT_COMPLETION]
    description: >
      CHAT_COMPLETION. Answers a message directly and conversationally, the
      way a chat assistant would, with no preamble. A "will X happen"
      question is answered with a verdict word (Likely, Unlikely, Uncertain)
      followed by the reason. Params: message (required; also accepted as
      prompt, text, question, query, or an OpenAI-style messages array whose
      last user turn is answered).
  - path: /news-search
    external_path: /news-search
    method: GET
    intents: [NEWS_SEARCH]
    description: >
      NEWS_SEARCH. Answers "what's the latest on the trade talks", "has the
      company announced results yet" from a live news-focused web search at
      request time, with sources named. Params: query (required; also q,
      question, topic, text, search, keywords, subject, category),
      max_results (optional, 1-20, default 5; also max, limit), recent_days
      (optional, default 7), country and language (optional hints).
  - path: /news-headlines
    external_path: /news-headlines
    method: GET
    intents: [NEWS_HEADLINES]
    description: >
      NEWS_HEADLINES. Answers "what are today's headlines on the election",
      "top news about the central bank". Returns a short list of current
      headlines on a named topic, each with its source URL. Params: topic
      (required; also query, q, question, category, subject, keywords; a
      whole question such as "What are the top news headlines about X
      today?" is accepted), max_results (optional, 1-10, default 6; also
      max, limit, count). Returns headlines as [{title, source, published,
      url}].
  - path: /fact-check
    external_path: /fact-check
    method: GET
    intents: [FACT_CHECK]
    description: >
      FACT_CHECK. Answers "is it true that X", "fact check this claim: ...".
      Checks a stated claim against live web sources and returns a
      True/False/Unverified verdict with the reasoning and sources behind it.
      Params: claim (required; also statement, text, query, q, question).
      Returns verdict (True, False, Mostly True, Mostly False, Misleading,
      Unverified) and the graded answer leads with that verdict word.
  - path: /sentiment-analyze
    external_path: /sentiment-analyze
    method: GET
    intents: [SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS]
    description: >
      SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS. Answers "is this review positive or negative",
      "what's the sentiment of this message". Classifies text as exactly one
      of Positive, Negative, Neutral or Mixed, with a short reason. Also
      answers "what is the general sentiment toward X" for a named company,
      token or event. Params: text (required; also accepted as content,
      review, message or comment).
  - path: /content-moderate
    external_path: /content-moderate
    method: GET
    intents: [CONTENT_MODERATION]
    description: >
      CONTENT_MODERATION. Answers "does this text violate policy", "is this
      message safe to post". Judges text as Safe or Flagged against common
      platform policies (hate speech, harassment, threats, illegal activity),
      with a short reason naming the concern. Params: text (required; also
      accepted as content, message, comment or post).
  - path: /cve-lookup
    external_path: /cve-lookup
    method: GET
    intents: [CVE_LOOKUP]
    description: >
      CVE_LOOKUP. Answers "what is CVE-2021-44228", "known vulnerabilities in
      log4j". Takes a CVE id or a keyword and returns matching vulnerability
      records from the National Vulnerability Database, with description,
      severity score, and references. Params: cve (required, a CVE id such
      as "CVE-2021-44228", a sentence containing one, or a product keyword
      such as "log4j"; also accepted as cve_id, id, vulnerability, query or
      question).
  - path: /telegraph-knowledge
    external_path: /telegraph-knowledge
    method: GET
    intents: [TELEGRAPH_KNOWLEDGE]
    description: >
      TELEGRAPH_KNOWLEDGE. Answers general-knowledge questions and questions
      about Telegraph Protocol itself, grounded against telegraphprotocol.com
      for protocol-specific questions rather than guessing about a protocol
      the model was not trained on. Params: question (required, also
      accepted as query, q, text, input).
  - path: /text-summarize
    external_path: /text-summarize
    method: GET
    intents: [TEXT_SUMMARIZATION]
    description: >
      TEXT_SUMMARIZATION. Summarizes supplied text to a given length or
      style, or a sensible default when none is named. Params: text
      (required), length (optional, e.g. "50 words" or "one sentence").
  - path: /chatbot-conversation
    external_path: /chatbot-conversation
    method: GET
    intents: [CHATBOT_CONVERSATION]
    description: >
      CHATBOT_CONVERSATION. Replies to a chat message, using a supplied
      messages/history array as context when given. Params: message
      (required), messages (optional, a JSON array of {role, content} turns,
      also accepted as history).
  - path: /semantic-similarity
    external_path: /semantic-similarity
    method: GET
    intents: [SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY]
    description: >
      SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY. Returns a 0-1 semantic similarity score and a
      short reason for two supplied texts. Params: text1, text2 (required,
      also accepted as a and b).
  - path: /grammar-spell-check
    external_path: /grammar-spell-check
    method: GET
    intents: [GRAMMAR_SPELL_CHECK]
    description: >
      GRAMMAR_SPELL_CHECK. Returns corrected text plus a count and list of
      the grammar and spelling fixes made. Params: text (required).
  - path: /ai-text-detect
    external_path: /ai-text-detect
    method: GET
    intents: [AI_TEXT_DETECTION]
    description: >
      AI_TEXT_DETECTION. Returns an approximate self-assessment of how
      likely supplied text is AI-generated, with named cues and an honest
      disclaimer that this is a language-model estimate, not a certified
      detector. Params: text (required).
  - path: /research-query
    external_path: /research-query
    method: GET
    intents: [RESEARCH_QUERY]
    description: >
      RESEARCH_QUERY. Answers an open research question from live web
      sources in one well-sourced paragraph. Params: query (required, also
      accepted as q, question, topic, text, research, search, prompt,
      subject), max_results (optional, 1-20, default 6).
  - path: /threat-intelligence
    external_path: /threat-intelligence
    method: GET
    intents: [THREAT_INTELLIGENCE]
    description: >
      THREAT_INTELLIGENCE. Given an IP, domain, file hash, CVE id, or threat
      actor/malware family name, reports whether it is a known threat:
      malicious/clean verdict and pulse count from AlienVault OTX for
      IPs/domains/hashes, exploitation status and CVSS severity from
      CIRCL/NVD for CVE ids, or a web-search-sourced profile for actor and
      malware-family names. Params: indicator (required, also accepted as
      ioc, ip, domain, hash, cve, actor, query, q, question, text, input).
  - path: /package-status
    external_path: /package-status
    method: GET
    intents: [PACKAGE_STATUS]
    description: >
      PACKAGE_STATUS. Given a shipment tracking number, reports its current
      status via live web search, since no free universal carrier API
      exists; answers honestly when no authoritative status can be found
      rather than guessing. Params: tracking_number (required, also accepted
      as tracking, tracking_id, number, package_id, query, q, question,
      text, input).
  - path: /url-scan
    external_path: /url-scan
    method: GET
    intents: [URL_SCAN]
    description: >
      URL_SCAN. Given a URL, returns a Safe/Suspicious/Unknown verdict
      combining live reachability and redirect-chain checking, TLS
      certificate validity, and a web-search reputation check for
      phishing/malware/scam reports. Params: url (required, also accepted as
      link, website, target, query, q, question, text, input).
  - path: /currency-exchange
    external_path: /currency-exchange
    method: GET
    intents: [CURRENCY_EXCHANGE]
    description: >
      CURRENCY_EXCHANGE. Answers "how much is 100 dollars in euros",
      "convert 50 GBP to JPY", using live ECB reference rates. Params: from,
      to (currency codes or names such as "dollars", "euros"), amount
      (optional, default 1).
  - path: /fx-now
    external_path: /fx-now
    method: GET
    intents: [FX_NOW]
    description: >
      FX_NOW. Answers "what is the USD to EUR rate right now", "current GBP
      JPY exchange rate", "how much is 250 dollars in naira today" with the
      current mid-market rate from a live FX feed covering 166 currencies,
      falling back to the ECB reference rate. Params: from (also base), to
      (also symbols, quote_currency), both currency codes or names such as
      "dollars", "euros"; amount (optional, default 1); or the whole question
      as query.
  - path: /sanctions-screening
    external_path: /sanctions-screening
    method: GET
    intents: [SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH]
    description: >
      SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH. Answers "is John Doe sanctioned", "check
      this company against the OFAC list". Screens a name against the US
      Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list with fuzzy matching.
      Params: name (required, a person or entity name).
  - path: /vulnerability-triage
    external_path: /vulnerability-triage
    method: GET
    intents: [VULNERABILITY_TRIAGE]
    description: >
      VULNERABILITY_TRIAGE. Answers "how urgent is CVE-2021-44228", "should
      I patch log4j now". Same CIRCL/NVD CVE data as CVE_LOOKUP, framed as a
      triage decision: severity tier, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
      status, and a recommended remediation urgency. Params: cve (required,
      a CVE id or product keyword).
  - path: /sports-score
    external_path: /sports-score
    method: GET
    intents: [SPORTS_SCORE]
    description: >
      SPORTS_SCORE. Answers "what is the score of the Lakers game". Most
      recent or in-progress score for a named team, via TheSportsDB, with a
      live web-search fallback for teams outside its coverage. Params: team
      (required, a club or franchise name).
  - path: /game-result
    external_path: /game-result
    method: GET
    intents: [GAME_RESULT]
    description: >
      GAME_RESULT. Answers "who won the Knicks game". Winner of a named
      team's most recently completed match, via TheSportsDB, with a live
      web-search fallback for teams outside its coverage. Params: team
      (required, a club or franchise name).
  - path: /route-eta
    external_path: /route-eta
    method: GET
    intents: [ROUTE_ETA]
    description: >
      ROUTE_ETA. Answers "how long to drive from London to Paris", "what is
      the distance between Miami and Orlando". Driving distance and
      estimated travel time via OSRM, with a route that can only be
      completed by ferry named honestly rather than reported as an ordinary
      driving time. Params: origin, destination (required, place names or
      "lat,lon"), mode (optional, driving only; other modes are refused
      honestly).
  - path: /regulatory-filing-monitor
    external_path: /regulatory-filing-monitor
    method: GET
    intents: [REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR]
    description: >
      REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR. Answers "will the FDA fine this company",
      "has this drug had a warning filed against it". Searches the US
      Federal Register for real, published filings and notices matching a
      named company, product, drug, device, or industry concern, reporting
      what has actually been filed rather than predicting future action.
      Params: company (required, also accepted as product, drug, device,
      or concern).
  - path: /credit-score-verify
    external_path: /credit-score-verify
    method: GET
    intents: [CREDIT_SCORE_VERIFY]
    description: >
      CREDIT_SCORE_VERIFY. Answers "is this a registered business",
      "verify this company's legal entity status". Checks a company name
      against the GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier registry: whether it has a
      registered LEI, its legal name, jurisdiction, and status. States
      plainly that LEI registration is not itself a credit score. Params:
      company (required).
  - path: /macro-economic-indicator
    external_path: /macro-economic-indicator
    method: GET
    intents: [MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR]
    description: >
      MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR. Answers "what is Japan's inflation rate",
      "how fast is the US economy growing". Reads GDP growth, inflation, or
      unemployment for a named country from World Bank data. Params:
      country (required, name or ISO code), economic_indicator (required,
      also accepted as indicator; GDP growth, inflation, or unemployment).
  - path: /weather-forecast-verify
    external_path: /weather-forecast-verify
    method: GET
    intents: [WEATHER_FORECAST_VERIFY]
    description: >
      WEATHER_FORECAST_VERIFY. Answers "what was the actual weather in
      London on August 1st". Reports what actually happened at a named
      place on a past date, from Open-Meteo's historical archive, distinct
      from WEATHER_FORECAST's forward-looking forecast; a date that is
      today or in the future is refused honestly. Params: location
      (required), date (required, YYYY-MM-DD, must be in the past).
  - path: /customer-ticket-resolution
    external_path: /customer-ticket-resolution
    method: GET
    intents: [CUSTOMER_TICKET_RESOLUTION]
    description: >
      CUSTOMER_TICKET_RESOLUTION. Answers "how do I fix this error", given a
      described technical problem. Searches live web sources for a known
      fix or resolution and reports it, sources named, or says honestly
      that none was found. Params: ticket (required, also accepted as
      description, issue, problem, error, or error_message).
  - path: /return-policy-verify
    external_path: /return-policy-verify
    method: GET
    intents: [RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY]
    description: >
      RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY. Answers "what is Costco's return policy". Given
      a retailer name, finds and reports that retailer's actual return
      policy (window, conditions) from a live search, sources named. Params:
      retailer (required, also accepted as store, merchant, or brand),
      product (optional purchase context).
  - path: /task-execution-quality
    external_path: /task-execution-quality
    method: GET
    intents: [TASK_EXECUTION_QUALITY]
    description: >
      TASK_EXECUTION_QUALITY. Given a task description and a produced
      result, judges whether the result actually satisfies the task
      (satisfies, partially_satisfies, or fails), with a reason. Params:
      task (required, also accepted as task_description or instructions),
      result (required, also accepted as output or response).
  - path: /carrier-serviceability
    external_path: /carrier-serviceability
    method: GET
    intents: [CARRIER_SERVICEABILITY]
    description: >
      CARRIER_SERVICEABILITY. Answers "does UPS deliver to this ZIP code".
      Given an address or ZIP code and optionally a carrier name, reports
      whether that carrier serves the area. Params: zip_code (required,
      also accepted as address), carrier (optional).
  - path: /delivery-window-verify
    external_path: /delivery-window-verify
    method: GET
    intents: [DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY]
    description: >
      DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY. Answers "how long does FedEx ground take from
      New York to LA". Given an origin, destination, and carrier/service
      level, estimates a realistic delivery window, honestly caveated as an
      estimate, not a guarantee. Params: origin, destination (optional,
      also accepted together as route), carrier (optional), service
      (optional, e.g. ground, express, overnight).
  - path: /payment-method-verify
    external_path: /payment-method-verify
    method: GET
    intents: [PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY]
    description: >
      PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY. Answers "what card network is this BIN",
      "is this a Visa or Mastercard number". Identifies the card network
      and, where possible, issuing bank and country from a card's leading
      digits (the BIN), a public and static lookup; states plainly that
      full card validity cannot be confirmed without processor access.
      Params: card_number (required, also accepted as payment_method for a
      network or app name).
  - path: /invoice-ledger-reconcile
    external_path: /invoice-ledger-reconcile
    method: GET
    intents: [INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE]
    description: >
      INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE. Given two described figures or a described
      invoice/ledger discrepancy, reconciles what can be reconciled from
      arithmetic and the stated facts alone; states plainly this is not a
      lookup against any real ledger system. Params: description (required,
      also accepted as invoice, ledger, or discrepancy).
  - path: /fraud-query
    external_path: /fraud-query
    method: POST
    intents: [FRAUD_DETECTION]
    description: >
      FRAUD_DETECTION. Answers "was BitConnect a scam", "is this scheme
      fraudulent", "what happened in the FTX fraud". Assesses how likely a
      named entity, scheme or action is to be fraudulent, answering from
      source-backed fraud knowledge rather than speculation, and returning
      INCONCLUSIVE rather than guessing when the record does not support a
      verdict. JSON body: { "query": "..." } (8 to 1000 characters).
  - path: /assess-wallet
    external_path: /assess-wallet
    method: GET
    intents: [FRAUD_DETECTION]
    description: >
      FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address. Answers "is 0xabc... a scam
      wallet", "how risky is this address", "is it safe to receive funds
      from this wallet". Returns a 0-1 risk score with named contributing
      signals, checked against a built-in registry of over 2,600 known
      entities (OFAC-sanctioned addresses, reported scam addresses, exchange
      and bridge wallets, mixers and burn addresses) so that known-legitimate
      infrastructure is not flagged as fraud. Risk and confidence are
      reported separately: a low-risk verdict from bounded scanning is
      returned as low risk with low confidence rather than overstated.
      Params: wallet (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters).
  - path: /assess-wallet
    external_path: /assess-wallet
    method: POST
    intents: [FRAUD_DETECTION]
    description: >
      FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address, identical to the GET form
      above and accepting the address in a JSON body instead of the query
      string. JSON body: { "wallet": "0x..." }.
  - path: /url-safe
    external_path: /url-safe
    method: GET
    intents: [URL_SAFE]
    description: >
      URL_SAFE. Given a URL, checks it against URLhaus, VirusTotal, and
      reputation services, returning Safe/Suspicious/Unknown with detection count.
      URLhaus provides free malicious URL database checks. VirusTotal returns
      multi-engine detection count. Web reputation search provides additional context.
      Params: url (required, also accepted as link, website, target, query, q,
      question, text, input).
  - path: /malware-detection
    external_path: /malware-detection
    method: GET
    intents: [MALWARE_DETECTION]
    description: >
      MALWARE_DETECTION. Given a domain, IP address, or file hash, checks it
      against VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, and AlienVault OTX reputation databases,
      returning threat level (None/Low/Medium/High/Critical) and match count.
      VirusTotal provides multi-engine detections for all indicator types.
      AbuseIPDB provides IP abuse confidence scoring. OTX provides free threat
      intelligence pulses. Params: indicator (required, an IP address, domain,
      or file hash, also accepted as ioc, ip, domain, hash, query, q, question,
      text, input).
  - path: /dns-check
    external_path: /dns-check
    method: GET
    intents: [DNS_RECORD_LOOKUP]
    description: >
      DNS_RECORD_LOOKUP. Answers "what are the DNS records for example.com",
      "what DNS entries does this domain have". Takes a hostname and returns
      A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, and SOA records queried live at request
      time using native DNS resolution. Params: hostname (required, a bare
      domain name like "example.com"; also accepted as domain, host, url, or
      a whole question naming the domain).
  - path: /threat-ip-reputation
    external_path: /threat-ip-reputation
    method: GET
    intents: [THREAT_IP_REPUTATION]
    description: >
      THREAT_IP_REPUTATION. Answers "is this IP address malicious",
      "is example.com a known threat domain", "what is the reputation of
      this IP". Takes an IP address or domain and returns threat assessment
      from AlienVault OTX and AbuseIPDB free APIs (no key required for OTX;
      AbuseIPDB key optional and rate-limited). Confidence scales with number
      of sources that returned data. Params: ip or domain (required; also
      accepted as indicator, ioc, host, query, q, or question).

  - path: /token-total-supply
    external_path: /token-total-supply
    method: GET
    intents: [TOKEN_TOTAL_SUPPLY_VERIFY]
    description: >
      TOKEN_TOTAL_SUPPLY_VERIFY. Answers "what is the total supply of USDC
      on Ethereum", "verify the supply of token 0xA0b8... at block
      23000000". Reads totalSupply(), decimals() and symbol() straight from
      the chain and returns total_supply (human units), total_supply_raw
      (the exact on-chain integer), decimals, symbol and block. Params:
      token (a 0x contract address, or a symbol such as USDC, USDT, DAI,
      WETH), chain (also venue or network: ethereum, eth-mainnet, 1, base,
      arbitrum, polygon, avalanche; default ethereum), block (optional
      block number, default latest).
  - path: /corporate-registry
    external_path: /corporate-registry
    method: GET
    intents: [CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP]
    description: >
      CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP. Answers "what is the registered address
      and incorporation status of Acme Inc. in Delaware", "is SpaceX an
      active company". Looks the company up in GLEIF, the global Legal
      Entity Identifier register: legal name, LEI, active status
      (status_active 1 or 0), jurisdiction, registered and headquarters
      address, creation date. Says plainly when no record exists. Params:
      name (also company, entity, legal_name; the company name),
      jurisdiction (optional, a state or country), or the whole question as
      query.
  - path: /email-security
    external_path: /email-security
    method: GET
    intents: [EMAIL_SECURITY]
    description: >
      EMAIL_SECURITY. Answers "is gmail.com protected against email
      spoofing", "check SPF, DKIM and DMARC for example.com". Reads the
      domain's live DNS (MX, SPF with redirects followed, DMARC policy,
      DKIM at common selectors, MTA-STS) and grades it Strong, Good, Weak
      or Unprotected with the specific gaps. Params: domain (a bare domain,
      also email, name or host; an email address works too), or the whole
      question as query.
  - path: /mining-hashprice
    external_path: /mining-hashprice
    method: GET
    intents: [MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY]
    description: >
      MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY. Answers "what is the Bitcoin hashprice at
      block 800000", "current hashprice". Computes hashprice in sats per
      PH/s per day (hashprice_sats_per_ph_s_day) from the block's coinbase
      reward and difficulty: reward x 144 / (difficulty x 2^32 / 600 /
      1e15), plus the fee-free figure and implied network hashrate. Params:
      height (a block height, or latest; also block).
  - path: /security-review
    external_path: /security-review
    method: GET
    intents: [SECURITY_REVIEW]
    description: >
      SECURITY_REVIEW. Reviews supplied code, configuration or a system
      description for security weaknesses. The answer leads with a verdict
      (Secure, Needs changes, Insecure), then the most serious issues with
      CWE/OWASP category and the concrete fix. Params: code (also snippet,
      config, diff, description), or the whole request as query.
  - path: /llm-output-evaluation
    external_path: /llm-output-evaluation
    method: GET
    intents: [LLM_OUTPUT_EVALUATION]
    description: >
      LLM_OUTPUT_EVALUATION. Grades a language model's answer for accuracy,
      completeness, relevance and clarity. The answer leads with a rating
      (Excellent, Good, Acceptable, Poor, Fails) and "Score: N/10", then the
      specific strengths and errors. Params: prompt (the original question),
      output (also response, answer, completion; the model answer to grade),
      reference (optional expected answer), criteria (optional), or all of it
      as query.
  - path: /contract-obligation-audit
    external_path: /contract-obligation-audit
    method: GET
    intents: [CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT]
    description: >
      CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT. Audits contract obligations: who owes what
      by when, and, given performance facts, whether each was met. The
      answer leads with a verdict (Compliant, Partially compliant,
      Non-compliant, Unclear) and cites the clause wording. Params: contract
      (also clause, agreement), obligation (optional), facts (also evidence,
      performance; optional), or the whole request as query.
  - path: /code-generation
    external_path: /code-generation
    method: GET
    intents: [CODE_GENERATION]
    description: >
      CODE_GENERATION. Writes complete, runnable code for an instruction, in
      the requested language (Python by default), as one fenced code block
      followed by a short note. Params: instruction (also task, spec,
      description), language (optional), or the whole request as query.
  - path: /code-review
    external_path: /code-review
    method: GET
    intents: [CODE_REVIEW]
    description: >
      CODE_REVIEW. Reviews supplied code or a diff for correctness bugs,
      security, performance and readability. The answer leads with a
      verdict (Approve, Request changes, Comment), then the findings in
      severity order with concrete fixes. Params: code (also diff, patch,
      snippet), language (optional), focus (optional), or the whole request
      as query.
  - path: /text-authenticity
    external_path: /text-authenticity
    method: GET
    intents: [TEXT_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK]
    description: >
      TEXT_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK. Judges whether a text is authentic, genuinely
      from its attributed source and not fabricated, altered or
      machine-generated to deceive. The answer leads with a verdict
      (Authentic, Likely authentic, Likely fabricated, Fabricated,
      Unverifiable) and the strongest reasons. Params: text (also content,
      passage, quote), source or author (optional attribution), or the whole
      request as query.

# input_schema/output_schema are top-level-only fields, documentation
# surfaced to callers rather than a per-endpoint validator (confirmed
# against docs.telegraphprotocol.com/docs/miners/yaml-config). One shared
# object across all four endpoints below — fields not relevant to a given
# endpoint (e.g. tx_hash on /gas-price) are simply absent from that
# endpoint's actual response, not present-but-null.
input_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    tx_hash:
      type: string
      pattern: "^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$"
      description: EVM transaction hash to look up. Used by /check-tx only.
    address:
      type: string
      pattern: "^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$"
      description: EVM address to check. Used by /wallet-balance only.
    token:
      type: string
      pattern: "^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$"
      description: >
        ERC-20 token contract address. Required on /token-holders.
        Optional on /wallet-balance (switches to ERC-20 balance instead of
        native). Required alongside price_chain on /crypto-price's
        chain_token mode.
    chain:
      type: string
      enum: [eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon]
      default: eth
      description: >
        Which chain to query. Defaults to eth if omitted. Used by
        /check-tx, /gas-price, /wallet-balance, /token-holders only —
        not used by /tvl or /crypto-price, which take tvl_chain /
        price_chain instead (see below).
    protocol:
      type: string
      description: DefiLlama protocol slug, e.g. "uniswap". Used by /tvl only. Exactly one of protocol/tvl_chain required for /tvl.
    tvl_chain:
      type: string
      description: >
        Free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "Ethereum" (not restricted to
        the `chain` enum above — DefiLlama covers ~460 chains). Used by
        /tvl only. Exactly one of protocol/tvl_chain required for /tvl.
    coin_id:
      type: string
      description: >
        CoinGecko coin id, e.g. "bitcoin". Used by /crypto-price only.
        Exactly one of coin_id / (price_chain+token) required for
        /crypto-price.
    price_chain:
      type: string
      description: >
        Free-text DefiLlama chain name for an on-chain token price lookup,
        e.g. "ethereum" (same namespace as tvl_chain, separate field since
        it's paired with `token` rather than used alone). Used by
        /crypto-price only, together with `token`.
    ticker:
      type: string
      description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. "AAPL". Required on /stock-price only.
    domain:
      type: string
      description: >
        Host to check on /ssl-check. A bare hostname ("example.com") is the
        canonical form, but a full URL, a host:port pair, or a whole
        question naming the domain are all accepted and reduced to the
        hostname.
    location:
      type: string
      description: >
        Place to forecast for, on /weather-forecast and /storm-alert, or to
        verify actual past conditions for, on /weather-forecast-verify. A
        place name ("London"), a "lat,lon" pair ("51.5,-0.13"), or the
        whole question ("Will it rain in London tomorrow?"), in which case
        the day or window and the aspect asked about are read from it too.
    when:
      type: string
      description: >
        Optional on /weather-forecast and /storm-alert. The day or window
        asked about: today, tonight, tomorrow, a weekday name, this
        weekend, this week, next week, or "the next N days"/"the next N
        hours". Overrides whatever the question itself implies.
    focus:
      type: string
      enum: [rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature]
      description: >
        Optional on /weather-forecast. Which aspect the answer should lead
        with. Read from the question when omitted.
    days:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 16
      description: Forecast length in days on /weather-forecast. Defaults to 3, or to what the question asks for.
    hours:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 384
      description: Window length in hours on /storm-alert, counted from the current hour. Defaults to 48.
    ip:
      type: string
      description: >
        IPv4 or IPv6 address to locate on /ip-geolocate, e.g. "8.8.8.8" or
        "2001:4860:4860::8888". A whole question containing one is also
        accepted.
    topic:
      type: string
      description: >
        Research topic to search for on /academic-search. A whole question
        is accepted, and a date range stated in it ("since 2020") is
        applied. On /news-headlines, the topic to list current headlines
        on.
    from_year:
      type: integer
      description: Earliest publication year on /academic-search. Read from the question when omitted.
    to_year:
      type: integer
      description: Latest publication year on /academic-search. Read from the question when omitted.
    limit:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 25
      description: How many papers to return on /academic-search. Defaults to 5.
    query:
      type: string
      description: >
        The whole question to answer on /web-search and /research-query,
        where it is the primary parameter rather than an alias. Also the
        general factual fraud question for /fraud-query, and a fallback
        alias for the main parameter on /ssl-check, /weather-forecast,
        /storm-alert, /ip-geolocate, /academic-search, /threat-intelligence,
        /package-status and /url-scan, so a caller that forwards the raw
        question under a generic name is still answered rather than refused.
    max_results:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 20
      description: >
        How many web sources to draw on for /web-search (default 5) or
        /research-query (default 6).
    topic_mode:
      type: string
      enum: [general, news, finance]
      description: >
        Which search index /web-search should use. Read from the wording of
        the question when omitted: current-events phrasing selects news and
        markets phrasing selects finance.
    wallet:
      type: string
      pattern: "^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$"
      description: Ethereum address assessed by /assess-wallet.
    url:
      type: string
      description: >
        Full http or https URL to fetch on /content-extract, or to assess
        for safety on /url-scan. A whole question containing one is also
        accepted; also accepted as link, website or target on /url-scan.
    text:
      type: string
      description: >
        Text to classify on /text-classify, to transform on
        /language-generate, to summarize on /text-summarize, or to check on
        /grammar-spell-check and /ai-text-detect.
    labels:
      type: string
      description: >
        Comma-separated candidate categories on /text-classify. When
        supplied, the answer must pick exactly one of these.
    prompt:
      type: string
      description: Instruction to write to on /text-generate.
    target:
      type: string
      description: >
        Target language, tone, or style on /language-generate. Also read
        from an instruction inside `text` when omitted.
    max_sources:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 20
      description: How many web sources to draw on for /research-synthesis. Defaults to 10.
    chains:
      type: string
      description: >
        Comma-separated list of chains to check on /cross-chain-state.
        Defaults to every RPC-enabled chain when omitted.
    message:
      type: string
      description: >
        Message to reply to on /chat-complete or /chatbot-conversation. Also
        accepted as an alias of text on /sentiment-analyze and
        /content-moderate.
    messages:
      type: string
      description: >
        /chat-complete and /chatbot-conversation alternative to message: an
        OpenAI-style JSON array of {role, content} turns. The last user turn
        is answered. Also accepted as history on /chatbot-conversation.
    target_language:
      type: string
      description: Alias of target on /language-translate. Also accepted as to, language, or langpair ("en|de").
    content:
      type: string
      description: Alias of text on /text-classify, /sentiment-analyze and /content-moderate.
    review:
      type: string
      description: Alias of text on /sentiment-analyze.
    categories:
      type: string
      description: Alias of labels on /text-classify.
    claim:
      type: string
      description: Claim to fact-check on /fact-check.
    cve:
      type: string
      description: >
        CVE id (e.g. "CVE-2021-44228"), a question containing one, or a
        product keyword to search on /cve-lookup or /vulnerability-triage.
        Also read from cve_id, id, vulnerability, query and question.
    cve_id:
      type: string
      description: Alias for cve on /cve-lookup.
    question:
      type: string
      description: >
        A question to answer on /telegraph-knowledge. Also accepted as
        query, q, text or input.
    length:
      type: string
      description: >
        Optional target length or style for /text-summarize, e.g. "50 words"
        or "one sentence".
    text1:
      type: string
      description: First text to compare on /semantic-similarity. Also accepted as a.
    text2:
      type: string
      description: Second text to compare on /semantic-similarity. Also accepted as b.
    indicator:
      type: string
      description: >
        IP address, domain, file hash, CVE id, or threat actor/malware
        family name to check on /threat-intelligence. Also accepted as ioc,
        ip, domain, hash, cve, or actor.
    tracking_number:
      type: string
      description: >
        Carrier shipment tracking number on /package-status. Also accepted
        as tracking, tracking_id, number, or package_id.
    from:
      type: string
      description: >
        Source currency code or name on /currency-exchange, e.g. "USD" or
        "dollars". Also accepted as an alias of origin on /route-eta.
    to:
      type: string
      description: >
        Target currency code or name on /currency-exchange, e.g. "EUR" or
        "euros". Also accepted as an alias of destination on /route-eta and
        of target_language on /language-translate.
    amount:
      type: number
      description: Amount to convert on /currency-exchange. Defaults to 1.
    name:
      type: string
      description: Person or entity name to screen on /sanctions-screening.
    team:
      type: string
      description: Club or franchise name on /sports-score or /game-result.
    origin:
      type: string
      description: >
        Starting place name or "lat,lon" on /route-eta. Also accepted as
        from, start, or source. On /delivery-window-verify, the shipment's
        origin place (optional; a whole route description in `route` is
        also accepted).
    destination:
      type: string
      description: >
        Ending place name or "lat,lon" on /route-eta. Also accepted as to,
        end, or target. On /delivery-window-verify, the shipment's
        destination place (optional; a whole route description in `route`
        is also accepted).
    mode:
      type: string
      description: >
        Travel mode on /route-eta. Only driving is reliably available on the
        public routing server this endpoint uses; other modes are refused
        honestly. Also accepted as profile or travel_mode.
    company:
      type: string
      description: >
        Company, product, drug, device, or industry concern to search
        Federal Register filings for on /regulatory-filing-monitor, or a
        company name to verify against the GLEIF legal-entity registry on
        /credit-score-verify.
    economic_indicator:
      type: string
      description: >
        GDP growth, inflation, or unemployment on /macro-economic-indicator.
        Also accepted as indicator. Used with country.
    date:
      type: string
      description: >
        A past date (YYYY-MM-DD) to verify actual weather conditions for on
        /weather-forecast-verify. A date that is today or in the future is
        refused; use /weather-forecast for that instead.
    ticket:
      type: string
      description: >
        The described error or technical problem on
        /customer-ticket-resolution. Also accepted as description, issue,
        problem, error, or error_message.
    retailer:
      type: string
      description: >
        The retailer or store name on /return-policy-verify. Also accepted
        as store, merchant, or brand.
    task:
      type: string
      description: >
        The original task description on /task-execution-quality. Also
        accepted as task_description or instructions. Used with result.
    result:
      type: string
      description: >
        The produced result to assess against task on
        /task-execution-quality. Also accepted as output or response.
    zip_code:
      type: string
      description: >
        Address or ZIP code on /carrier-serviceability. Also accepted as
        address.
    carrier:
      type: string
      description: >
        Carrier name (e.g. UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL) on /carrier-serviceability
        and /delivery-window-verify. Optional on both.
    route:
      type: string
      description: >
        Free-text route description on /delivery-window-verify, when origin
        and destination are not given separately.
    service:
      type: string
      description: >
        Service level (e.g. ground, express, overnight) on
        /delivery-window-verify. Optional.
    card_number:
      type: string
      description: >
        Full or partial card number, or its leading 6-8 digits (the BIN), on
        /payment-method-verify.
    payment_method:
      type: string
      description: >
        Card network name or payment app name on /payment-method-verify.
        Alternative to card_number.
    description:
      type: string
      description: >
        Free-text description of the figures and any claimed discrepancy on
        /invoice-ledger-reconcile. Also accepted as invoice, ledger, or
        discrepancy.
    venue:
      type: string
      description: >
        Chain for /token-total-supply, same as chain (ethereum, eth-mainnet,
        or a chain id such as 1).
    block:
      type: string
      description: >
        Block number for /token-total-supply (default latest).
    height:
      type: string
      description: >
        Bitcoin block height for /mining-hashprice, or latest.
    jurisdiction:
      type: string
      description: >
        State or country the company is registered in, on
        /corporate-registry. Optional.
    code:
      type: string
      description: >
        Source code or a diff on /security-review and /code-review.
    instruction:
      type: string
      description: >
        What the code should do, on /code-generation.
    language:
      type: string
      description: >
        Programming language on /code-generation and /code-review.
    output:
      type: string
      description: >
        The model answer to grade on /llm-output-evaluation.
    reference:
      type: string
      description: >
        Optional expected answer on /llm-output-evaluation.
    contract:
      type: string
      description: >
        Contract text or clause on /contract-obligation-audit.
    facts:
      type: string
      description: >
        What actually happened, on /contract-obligation-audit. Optional.
output_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    answer:
      type: string
      description: >
        The graded answer: one self-contained sentence stating the result and
        the facts behind it, on every endpoint. This is the field named by
        semantics.signal_mapping.label_field. It repeats `summary` unless a
        route supplies its own fuller wording (the fraud routes do).
    tx_hash:
      type: string
      description: /check-tx only.
    address:
      type: string
      description: /wallet-balance only.
    token:
      type: string
      description: /token-holders always; /wallet-balance only when the token param was supplied.
    chain:
      type: string
    query_type:
      type: string
      enum: [protocol, chain, protocol_chain, coin_id, chain_token]
      description: >
        /tvl and /crypto-price only. Which query mode the request used
        (protocol/chain for /tvl, coin_id/chain_token for /crypto-price).
    query:
      type: string
      description: >
        Echoes the main lookup value on routes that return it, including
        TVL, crypto, stock, weather and academic search.
    status:
      type: string
      description: >
        confirmed/reverted/pending/not_found/error on /check-tx; ok/error
        on /gas-price and /wallet-balance (live reads have no confirmation
        states); ok/not_found/error on /token-holders (not_found means the
        address isn't a known ERC-20 token on that chain, not a failure).
        Fraud routes may use Sentinel's named verdict. A Sentinel outage is
        inconclusive rather than a failed HTTP request.
        invalid_input can be returned by any endpoint and is an answer, not
        a failure: it means the parameters supplied could not identify
        anything to look up, and summary explains in plain language what the
        endpoint needs instead. It is returned with HTTP 200 and no error
        field, because the input was unusable rather than TxLens being
        unable to serve.
    summary:
      type: string
    confidence:
      type: number
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 1
    canonical:
      type: string
      description: >
        Compact deterministic one-line verdict summary, shape varies per
        endpoint (documented in each route's description).
    as_of:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: >
        ISO timestamp of the source reading on gas, balance, holders, TVL,
        crypto and stock routes. On /stock-price this is the provider's
        quote observation time and is null when the provider did not supply
        one; it is never replaced by the response retrieval time.
    from:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only.
    to:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only. Null for contract-creation transactions.
    value_wei:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only.
    value_eth:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only. Native-token value in human-readable units. The legacy field name is value_eth, including on Polygon where the native token is POL.
    method:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only. Decoded contract method name when available.
    method_signature:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only. Decoded contract method signature when available.
    method_selector:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only. First four calldata bytes for contract calls.
    block_number:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: Null while pending / no receipt yet, or if the block-number read failed best-effort.
    block_hash:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /check-tx only. Null while pending / no receipt yet.
    receipt_status:
      type: [string, "null"]
      enum: [success, failed, null]
      description: >
        /check-tx only. Explicit receipt outcome, independent of `status`.
        Null while pending / not found (no receipt exists yet).
    gas_price_wei:
      type: string
      description: /gas-price only.
    gas_price_gwei:
      type: number
      description: /gas-price only.
    fee_usd:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: >
        /gas-price only. Estimated USD cost of a standard 21,000-gas
        transfer at the current gas price. Null if the native token's USD
        price could not be looked up — gas_price_wei/gwei are still valid
        in that case.
    native_price_usd:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /gas-price only. USD price of the chain's native gas token used to compute fee_usd. Null under the same condition as fee_usd.
    balance_wei:
      type: string
      description: /wallet-balance only. Raw integer amount, native wei or the ERC-20's smallest unit depending on whether token was supplied.
    balance_native:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: >
        /wallet-balance only. Human-normalized amount. Always present for
        native balance; null for an ERC-20 balance if Blockscout didn't
        recognize the token (decimals unknown, balance_wei still valid).
    holders_count:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      description: /token-holders only. Null when status is not_found.
    token_name:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /token-holders always; /wallet-balance only when token was supplied.
    token_symbol:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /token-holders always; /wallet-balance and /crypto-price only when applicable.
    token_decimals:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      description: /wallet-balance only, when token was supplied. Null if Blockscout didn't recognize the token.
    tvl_usd:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /tvl only. Null when status is not_found.
    chain_tvl_usd:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /tvl only. Protocol TVL on the requested chain when both protocol and tvl_chain are supplied.
    protocol_total_tvl_usd:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /tvl only. Total protocol TVL across all chains when both protocol and tvl_chain are supplied.
    price_usd:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: >
        /crypto-price and /stock-price. On /stock-price this is populated
        only when the provider quote is denominated in USD; it is null for
        non-USD listings and when status is not_found.
    price:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /stock-price only. The listing price in the units named by currency.
    company_name:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /stock-price only. Provider-supplied company name, or null when the provider omitted it.
    change_24h_pct:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /crypto-price only. CoinPaprika 24-hour USD price change percentage when available.
    market_cap_usd:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /crypto-price only. Current CoinPaprika market capitalization when available.
    source_count:
      type: integer
      description: >
        On /crypto-price, the number of independent price feeds that
        answered. On /research-synthesis and /research-query, how many web
        sources the answer drew on.
    sources:
      type: array
      items:
        type: object
      description: >
        On /crypto-price, the independent price feeds that answered. On
        /web-search, /news-search and /fact-check, the pages the answer drew
        on, each carrying title, url, snippet and the provider's relevance
        score, in relevance order.
    price_source:
      type: string
      enum: [coinpaprika, defillama, twelve_data, yahoo_finance]
      description: >
        /crypto-price and /stock-price. Which upstream actually supplied
        the selected price.
    currency:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: >
        /stock-price only. Exact provider denomination, including case when
        it distinguishes units such as GBp (pence) from GBP (pounds).
    exchange:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /stock-price only. The exchange the ticker trades on.
    retrieved_at:
      type: string
      description: /stock-price only. ISO timestamp when TxLens retrieved the quote, distinct from provider observation time in as_of.
    valid:
      type: [boolean, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Null when status is unreachable (the handshake itself failed, so validity is unknown, not false).
    authorized:
      type: [boolean, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Whether Node's default trust store accepts the certificate chain.
    chain_complete:
      type: [boolean, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Null when the host is unreachable and the chain cannot be inspected.
    hostname_valid:
      type: [boolean, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Null when the host is unreachable and hostname validation cannot run.
    unreachable_reason:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Connection or DNS failure when the host cannot be inspected.
    authorization_error:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Reason authorized is false, e.g. a self-signed or expired certificate.
    issuer:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Certificate authority organization or common name.
    valid_from:
      type: string
      description: /ssl-check only. ISO timestamp of certificate issuance.
    valid_to:
      type: string
      description: /ssl-check only. ISO timestamp of certificate expiry.
    days_until_expiry:
      type: integer
      description: /ssl-check only. Negative if already expired.
    category:
      type: string
      enum: [valid, expired, self_signed, hostname_mismatch, untrusted]
      description: /ssl-check only. The named certificate verdict.
    chain_length:
      type: integer
      description: >
        /ssl-check only. How many certificates the server itself presented.
        Excludes the trust anchor the local store supplies, which the
        server did not send.
    matched_hostname:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Which name on the certificate the requested host matched, wildcards included. Null on a hostname mismatch.
    covers_hostnames:
      type: array
      items:
        type: string
      description: /ssl-check only. Every DNS name and IP the certificate covers.
    protocol:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. TLS version actually negotiated, e.g. TLSv1.3.
    cipher:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Cipher suite actually negotiated.
    protocol_deprecated:
      type: boolean
      description: /ssl-check only. True for TLS 1.0/1.1, which most modern clients refuse regardless of certificate validity.
    key_bits:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. Certificate public key size in bits.
    fingerprint_sha256:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ssl-check only. SHA-256 fingerprint of the leaf certificate.
    checked_at:
      type: string
      description: >
        ISO timestamp of the live read, on /ssl-check, /weather-forecast,
        /storm-alert, /ip-geolocate and /academic-search.
    location:
      type: string
      description: /weather-forecast and /storm-alert. The resolved place, as name, region, country.
    when:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /weather-forecast only. The day or window the answer covers, as understood from the request.
    focus:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /weather-forecast only. The aspect the answer leads with, as understood from the request.
    condition:
      type: string
      description: >
        On /weather-forecast, the expected condition in plain words, from
        the WMO weather code. On /weather-forecast-verify, the recorded
        condition for the verified past date.
    temp_min_c:
      type: number
      description: >
        On /weather-forecast, the lowest temperature across the forecast
        window. On /weather-forecast-verify, the recorded low for the
        verified past date. Celsius.
    temp_max_c:
      type: number
      description: >
        On /weather-forecast, the highest temperature across the forecast
        window. On /weather-forecast-verify, the recorded high for the
        verified past date. Celsius.
    precipitation_total_mm:
      type: number
      description: /weather-forecast only. Total precipitation across the window.
    precipitation_probability_max_pct:
      type: number
      description: /weather-forecast only. Peak chance of precipitation across the window.
    snowfall_total_cm:
      type: number
      description: /weather-forecast only. Total snowfall across the window.
    peak_wind_kmh:
      type: number
      description: /weather-forecast only. Highest sustained wind across the window.
    days:
      type: array
      items:
        type: object
      description: /weather-forecast only. Day-by-day breakdown of every field above.
    hours_assessed:
      type: integer
      description: /storm-alert only. Length of the assessed window in hours.
    window_start:
      type: string
      description: /storm-alert only. Local time of the first assessed hour. Starts at the current hour, not midnight.
    window_end:
      type: string
      description: /storm-alert only. Local time of the last assessed hour.
    peak_gust_kmh:
      type: number
      description: /storm-alert and /weather-forecast. Strongest wind gust in the window.
    peak_gust_time:
      type: string
      description: /storm-alert only. Local time of the strongest gust. Always inside the future window.
    max_wind_speed_kmh:
      type: [number, "null"]
      description: /storm-alert only. Strongest sustained wind in the window.
    wind_direction:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: >
        On /storm-alert, the prevailing wind direction at the peak, as a
        compass word. On /weather-check, the compass direction the wind is
        blowing from right now.
    beaufort_force:
      type: integer
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 12
      description: /storm-alert only. Beaufort force of the peak gust.
    beaufort_description:
      type: string
      description: /storm-alert only. That Beaufort force in plain words, e.g. "gale".
    thunderstorm_hours:
      type: integer
      description: /storm-alert only. Forecast hours with a thunderstorm in the window.
    severe_hail_hours:
      type: integer
      description: /storm-alert only. Forecast hours with a hail-bearing thunderstorm.
    recommended_action:
      type: string
      description: >
        On /storm-alert, the operational response the risk grade calls for.
        On /vulnerability-triage, the recommended remediation urgency.
    country:
      type: string
      description: >
        On /ip-geolocate, the country the address resolves to. On
        /macro-economic-indicator, the country the value applies to,
        echoed back from the resolved country name.
    country_code:
      type: string
      description: /ip-geolocate only. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.
    region:
      type: string
      description: /ip-geolocate only.
    city:
      type: string
      description: /ip-geolocate only. Approximate, see confidence.
    zip:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ip-geolocate only.
    latitude:
      type: number
      description: /ip-geolocate, /weather-forecast and /storm-alert.
    longitude:
      type: number
      description: /ip-geolocate, /weather-forecast and /storm-alert.
    timezone:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ip-geolocate, /weather-forecast and /storm-alert. IANA timezone name.
    isp:
      type: string
      description: /ip-geolocate only. Network operator.
    org:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ip-geolocate only. Registrant organization, when it differs from the operator.
    asn:
      type: [string, "null"]
      description: /ip-geolocate only. Autonomous system number and name.
    is_mobile:
      type: boolean
      description: /ip-geolocate only. Address belongs to a mobile carrier network.
