    is_proxy_or_vpn:
      type: boolean
      description: /ip-geolocate only. Address is a known proxy or VPN exit.
    is_hosting:
      type: boolean
      description: /ip-geolocate only. Address belongs to a hosting or datacenter network rather than a residential connection.
    total_matches:
      type: integer
      description: >
        On /academic-search, how many peer-reviewed articles matched, of
        which `papers` is the returned page. On /regulatory-filing-monitor,
        how many Federal Register documents matched.
    papers:
      type: array
      items:
        type: object
      description: >
        /academic-search only. Each entry carries title, year,
        citation_count, authors, venue, doi and abstract_snippet. Listed in
        relevance order.
    most_cited:
      type: [object, "null"]
      description: /academic-search only. Whichever returned paper carries the most citations. Reported alongside the results, not used to order them.
    from_year:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      description: /academic-search only. Earliest publication year applied, whether passed or read from the question.
    to_year:
      type: [integer, "null"]
      description: /academic-search only. Latest publication year applied, whether passed or read from the question.
    search_query:
      type: string
      description: >
        /web-search only. The text actually sent to the search index, after
        an instruction aimed at the miner ("search the web for ...") has
        been removed from the front of the question.
    topic:
      type: string
      enum: [general, news, finance]
      description: /web-search only. Which search index answered, whether passed as topic_mode or read from the question.
    result_count:
      type: integer
      description: >
        /web-search, /event-outcome, /news-search, /news-headlines and
        /cve-lookup. How many web sources or CVE records the answer drew on.
    provider:
      type: string
      description: /web-search only. Which search service supplied the answer.
    mode:
      type: string
      enum: [fraud_knowledge, wallet_risk]
    label:
      type: string
      description: Sentinel fraud verdict, also returned as status for TxLens compatibility.
    reason:
      type: string
      description: >
        Complete fraud answer or wallet-risk explanation. On
        /task-execution-quality, why the result was judged to satisfy or
        fail the task.
    assessment_status:
      type: string
      enum: [ASSESSED, LIMITED, INCONCLUSIVE]
    source:
      type: [object, string]
      description: >
        On several routes (/currency-exchange, /cve-lookup,
        /regulatory-filing-monitor, /credit-score-verify,
        /macro-economic-indicator, /weather-forecast-verify), a plain string
        naming the data provider. On the fraud/wallet-risk routes, an object
        with structured detail.
    wallet:
      type: string
    risk_score:
      type: number
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 1
      description: >
        Wallet fraud risk on /assess-wallet. On /storm-alert, weather
        disruption risk on the same 0-1 scale, for callers that threshold
        rather than branch on the named grade.
    risk_level:
      type: string
      enum: [LOW, ELEVATED, HIGH, NOT_APPLICABLE, MODERATE, SEVERE]
      description: >
        Named risk grade. LOW/ELEVATED/HIGH/NOT_APPLICABLE on
        /assess-wallet; LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/SEVERE on /storm-alert.
    reason_codes:
      type: array
      items:
        type: string
    evidence:
      type: array
      items:
        type: object
    coverage:
      type: object
    latency_ms:
      type: number
    analysis_tier:
      type: string

# Where TxLens reports failures inside its JSON body. message_path and
# code_path only make failures readable to callers; they do not change
# which calls count as failures.
#
# status_path is deliberately NOT declared. TxLens uses real HTTP status
# codes, and the docs say to omit status_path in that case. Declaring it
# here would be actively harmful: a successful lookup that legitimately
# answers "not_found" (a hash that is not on chain) carries
# status: not_found in a 200 response, and would be reclassified as a
# failed call.
errors:
  message_path: summary
  code_path: error

limitations:
  - code: MAX_PARAM_VALUE
    message: tx_hash must be exactly 66 characters (0x-prefixed, 64 hex characters).
    param: tx_hash
    property: length
    value_num: 66
    operator: eq
  - code: MAX_PARAM_VALUE
    message: address must be exactly 42 characters (0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters).
    param: address
    property: length
    value_num: 42
    operator: eq
  - code: MAX_PARAM_VALUE
    message: token must be exactly 42 characters (0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters).
    param: token

    value_num: 42

# Lets a contract reach txlens through an ERC-8183 job. Without a request
# mapping the node calls the first endpoint in this file with no parameters,
# so every job for any intent arrived at /check-tx empty and answered "no
# transaction hash was supplied". Reported by the Amanat miner author, whose
# storm contract hit it twice (Sireadell/onchain-tx pull request 1,
# 2026-09-07). The shape follows telegraphprotocol/telegraph-examples
# frontend/yaml/example-miner.yaml and the body form of the live, active
# amanat-weather-risk registration. The node matches each entry's endpoint

# weather-forecast-verify is never taken for weather-forecast.
